skill.name: mcp-builder
skill.description: Build Model Context Protocol servers with guidance for tools, resources, prompts, authentication, testing, and deployment.
skill.summary: Guide AI agents through secure MCP server design, implementation, testing, and deployment.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation placeholders, markdown formatting, or normal configuration examples. Confirmed issues remain in copyable examples: arbitrary file access, full environment exposure, path traversal in resource readers, and user-controlled URL fetching.

remediation.issue: Advanced server exposes arbitrary file reads and writes.
remediation.suggestion: Remove file_write from the default example or restrict file operations to a normalized allowlisted workspace.

remediation.issue: Resource examples can expose environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Never return dict(os.environ). Return only non-secret configuration keys and redact sensitive values.

remediation.issue: Resource readers allow path traversal through URI-derived paths.
remediation.suggestion: Normalize resolved paths and verify they remain inside the approved documentation or log directory.

remediation.issue: The production HTTP client fetches user-controlled URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Validate schemes, block private and local networks, and prefer an allowlist of approved domains.

content.user_title: Build MCP Servers for AI Tooling
content.value_statement: Teams need reliable patterns for connecting AI assistants to tools, APIs, and data sources. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through MCP server design, security, testing, and deployment.
actual_capabilities: Explains MCP concepts, server architecture, transports, tools, resources, and prompts.
Provides Python server patterns for tool registration, resource readers, prompts, and error handling.
Includes examples for REST API wrappers, database access, resource servers, and advanced multi-tool servers.
Covers authentication, secrets handling, URL validation, rate limiting, testing, debugging, and deployment.
Shows Claude Desktop configuration patterns for local MCP servers.
limitations: Example servers require review before production use.
It does not generate a complete server automatically without user direction.
Some examples use placeholder APIs, tokens, paths, and in-memory data.
Production safety depends on user-supplied validation, access controls, and deployment settings.

use_cases.title: Create Internal AI Tools
use_cases.description: Build MCP tools that let an assistant query approved internal services and return structured results.

use_cases.title: Expose Documentation Resources
use_cases.description: Design read-only MCP resources for product manuals, API references, and operational runbooks.

use_cases.title: Prepare Production Deployments
use_cases.description: Review authentication, rate limits, logging, monitoring, and deployment steps before releasing an MCP server.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic MCP Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a small MCP server in Python. It needs one safe tool, clear input validation, and local testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add API Tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan MCP tools for this external API. Include schemas, authentication handling, rate limits, errors, and tests for each tool.

prompt_templates.title: Design Resource Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Design read-only MCP resources for these files and documents. Include URI patterns, path restrictions, metadata, and cache behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this MCP server plan for production. Focus on secrets, filesystem access, network access, authentication, logging, monitoring, and deployment risk.

output_examples.input: Build an MCP server for a support knowledge base.
output: A resource design with approved document roots and URI patterns.
A tool list for search and article lookup with validated inputs.
A test plan using local fixtures and MCP inspector checks.

output_examples.input: Wrap a third-party issue tracker as MCP tools.
output: Tool definitions for search, read, create, and update operations.
Authentication guidance using environment variables or managed secrets.
Error handling guidance for rate limits, missing permissions, and invalid fields.

output_examples.input: Review my MCP server before deployment.
output: A prioritized checklist for authentication, authorization, and input validation.
A list of unsafe filesystem and network patterns to remove.
Deployment recommendations for logging, monitoring, and rollback.

best_practices: Validate all tool arguments before network, database, or filesystem access.
Store credentials in environment variables or managed secret stores.
Keep example code separated from production code and review every copy.
anti_patterns: Expose full environment variables through MCP resources.
Accept arbitrary file paths or URLs without allowlists.
Treat placeholder credentials as production secrets.

faq.question: Does this skill create an MCP server by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that an AI agent can adapt with your requirements.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows for MCP server planning and implementation.

faq.question: Can I use the examples in production?
faq.answer: Only after hardening. Review file access, network access, authentication, secrets, and resource exposure first.

faq.question: Does it support TypeScript?
faq.answer: It references TypeScript SDK resources, but the included implementation examples are mainly Python.

faq.question: What risks should I review first?
faq.answer: Review arbitrary file paths, user-controlled URLs, secrets handling, authentication, and environment exposure.

faq.question: Does it include testing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes unit testing, integration testing, inspector usage, and debugging guidance.
